Blocks.Text: Warning

Deprecation Notice:
The Marketing Version 202510 (Marketing October 2025) will be sunset on October 15, 2026. We recommend that you migrate to the latest versioned APIs to avoid disruptions. For information on all the supported versions, refer to the migrations documentation.
If you haven’t yet migrated and have questions, submit a request on the LinkedIn Developer Support Portal.
Using the /organizationalAuthorizations endpoint is optional; you may continue using /organizationAcls
Read more:

Role to Permission Mapping
Organization Authorization Actions
There are currently more than 100 features available across the LinkedIn ecosystem, and there are multiple feature sets for content creators.
Consider this workflow:

Five (5) Pages Partners.
Each Partner makes 20 checks across the Apps.
The manual procedure for feature checks for each new partner will multiply the effort required to administer or maintain user permissions by role.
This change includes newly added roles, which

Provide structure and granularity to page admin roles.
Provide instant access to new roles available in existing API.
Eliminates role-based permissions using /organizationAcls which provides too much privilege or restricts access.
Organization Authorizations provides a more granular delegation of access to company page management. User Roles may still be provisioned using /organizationAcls
/organizationAuthorizations exists as a convenient utility for permission checking, which is useful for permissions that span multiple roles.

Blocks.Section: Why would I spend resources to build a complex feature check?
SectionPath: Why would I spend resources to build a complex feature check?
Blocks.Text: Using /organizationAuthorizations eliminates the need to check multiple user roles, provides more granular page admin roles/permissions, and requires no code changes for newly added roles in the future.

LinkedIn anticipates a 20+ increase in Roles over the next few years for pages. To use /organizationAuthorizations you'll need to find the following existing roles and how they're mapped to the new endpoint.
Learn more:

Blocks.Section: How do I find an authenticated member’s organization role assignee?
SectionPath: How do I find an authenticated member’s organization role assignee?
Blocks.Text: You don't need to maintain a list of roles that have permissions, Users are allowed to continue using cURL /organizationAuthorizations -X GET method to determine if the member has a particular permission at an organization.
